title: Identifiers
subject: user-organization-mgmt
summary: Two different things, deliberately kept apart:

claims.text: **Login identifiers** — what you can type to sign in. Security-sensitive: verified, credential-bearing, owned by the identity provider. **Capped.**

**Contact addresses** — where the product reaches you. Unlimited, plain rows in the module's db (`user_contacts`: a `{ label, type, value }` payload + `isDefault`), no login power. The first login identifier seeds the DEFAULT contact at birth (once — contacts never sync with identifiers afterwards), and member lists show it. Contact management UI is a later stage.

reference.statement: Two different things, deliberately kept apart:

reference.topic: The slot model (and why a cap exists)

claims.text: Slot names are an **adapter detail** — the port speaks `{ type, value }` lists, the UI shows a list of addresses. Nothing outside `api/identity/kratos/` knows slots exist.
One password, one TOTP enrollment, one AAL per account — because all slots live on ONE identity. (The rejected alternative — one identity per email — would fragment MFA and password state.)
**Raising the cap is cheap**: adding another optional trait is a compatible schema change. Unlimited is impossible with Kratos identifier traits; genuinely unlimited addresses belong in contacts.

reference.statement: Kratos login identifiers must be discrete string traits declared in the identity schema — an array of emails cannot be a credential identifier. So "multiple emails" is modeled as fixed slots, every one a full first-class login identifier (password + code login, verification, recovery):

claims.text: **Add**: `port.addIdentifier(identityId, { type, value })` → first free slot; the address starts unverified; the caller then proves a code sent to it. Emails run the provider's verification flow; the provider's verification flow is email-only, so **phones prove possession via a code LOGIN** to the address (the same reroute recovery uses) — proving it marks the address verified and the incidental session is discarded. Re-adding your own unverified identifier just restarts verification (a resend).

**Remove**: slots re-compact (no holes). The service guards two things: the identifier is on the CALLER's account, and the account keeps at least one login identifier (zero is unrecoverable — nothing can ever start a session again). Whether the REMAINING identifiers stay usable in every membership context is the gate's job, not removal's: dropping the last identifier a context accepts succeeds, and the gate answers the next request with an `identifier_present` obligation for the types that context accepts (any one satisfies it).
**Uniqueness** is global across accounts (provider lookup by `credentials_identifier` covers every slot).
**Verification state** rides on the provider's `verifiable_addresses` — the gate's `identifier_verified` obligation asks "does the caller have a verified address of this type", satisfied by any slot.

reference.statement: The identity schema (`api/identity/kratos/infra/identity.schema.json`) is immutable per `$id` in spirit: adding OPTIONAL traits is compatible (existing identities still validate); renaming/removing/requiring traits needs a new versioned `$id` plus an identity migration. Traits stay minimal (identifier slots + `name`); everything else lives in module tables.
